title: A malformed or unsupported sidecar is rejected with its line or byte offset
description:
## Behavior
Apricity is strict: a sidecar it cannot trust is rejected with where the problem is (element path and line for `.alc`, byte offset for `.asd`) and what to do.

```gherkin
Feature: Malformed sidecars are rejected with their location

  Scenario: Warp markers out of order in an .alc
    Given an .alc whose 4th warp marker is earlier in seconds than its 3rd
    When I read it
    Then reading fails with "line 57: WarpMarkers/WarpMarker[4]: 12.40 s (beat 7) is before marker 3 (12.52 s, beat 6); markers must increase in both seconds and beats"

  Scenario: Warping on with fewer than two markers
    Given an .alc with warping on and one warp marker
    When I read it
    Then reading fails with a message naming the WarpMarkers element and "needs at least two warp markers"

  Scenario: A truncated .asd
    Given the reference "steady-120.wav.asd" cut short at byte 4000
    When I read it
    Then reading fails with "byte 4000: file ends inside the warp marker list"

  Scenario: An .asd from a version Apricity cannot read
    Given an .asd whose version marker is one Apricity does not know
    When I read it
    Then reading fails naming the version found and the versions supported
    And the message suggests saving the clip as an .alc instead

  Scenario: Not a sidecar at all
    Given a file named "x.alc" that is not gzip-compressed XML
    When I read it
    Then reading fails with "x.alc: not an .alc (expected gzip-compressed XML)"
```
